rose-circular-momentscurated\begin{aligned} \term{circularAngle}{\phi_i}&=m\,\theta_i,\qquad m=1\ \text{(directional) or } 2\ \text{(axial)}\\ \term{cosineSum}{C}&=\sum_i w_i\cos\phi_i,\qquad \term{sineSum}{S}=\sum_i w_i\sin\phi_i,\qquad \term{totalWeight}{W}=\sum_i w_i\\ \term{resultant}{R}&=\frac{\sqrt{C^2+S^2}}{W},\qquad \term{meanAngle}{\bar{\theta}}=\tfrac{1}{m}\operatorname{atan2}(S,C),\qquad V=1-R\\ \term{rayleighZ}{z}&=\frac{(\sum_i\cos\phi_i)^2+(\sum_i\sin\phi_i)^2}{\term{validCount}{n}}=n\,\bar{R}_0^2 \end{aligned}theta_i = atan2(dy, dx) of segment i, in [0, 2 pi) (axial: folded into [0, pi)); phi_i = m theta_i with m = 1 (directional) or 2 (axial). C = sum w_i cos(phi_i), S = sum w_i sin(phi_i), W = sum w_i over segments with positive finite length and weight. Mean angle = atan2(S, C) / m, resultant length R = sqrt(C^2 + S^2) / W, circular variance V = 1 - R, Rayleigh z = ((sum cos(phi_i))^2 + (sum sin(phi_i))^2) / n = n Rbar_0^2, using each of the n valid directions once, independently of descriptive weights. Rbar_0 is the unweighted resultant, distinct from the weighted R. This is not giddy Rose permutation inference; no p-value is returned. Bins are left-closed equal-width sectors of the period (2 pi, or pi when axial) holding the summed weight. C = sum w_i cos(phi_i), S = sum w_i sin(phi_i), W = sum w_i over segments with positive finite length and weight. Mean angle = atan2(S, C) / m, resultant length R = sqrt(C^2 + S^2) / W, circular variance V = 1 - R, Rayleigh z = ((sum cos(phi_i))^2 + (sum sin(phi_i))^2) / n = n Rbar_0^2, using each of the n valid directions once, independently of descriptive weights. Rbar_0 is the unweighted resultant, distinct from the weighted R. This is not giddy Rose permutation inference; no p-value is returned.
